article.headline: One Command Turns Claude Code Into a Video Production Studio
article.lede: Remotion, the React framework that replaces video-editing timelines with code, has released "Agent Skills" — structured instruction files that teach AI coding assistants how to write correct Remotion code from natural-language prompts. A single terminal command, `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills`, installs them into a project's `.claude/skills` directory, after which Claude Code can generate animated MP4s from a description alone. The announcement tweet shows the terminal session and a sample animation produced entirely through prompting.
article.body:
**Remotion** is a framework, now managed by Remotion AG, that treats video as a React application: developers write components whose output is a rendered video file rather than a web page. The appeal is reproducibility and scriptability — swap a data source, re-render, done — but the learning curve is real. Mastering the composition model, frame-based timing, and animation primitives like `interpolate` and `spring` takes time, and large language models historically produced plausible-looking Remotion code that failed at runtime.

Agent Skills are the framework's answer to that fragility. Technically they are plain-text instruction files — essentially curated best-practice prompts — that live in `.claude/skills` inside the project directory. When Claude Code picks up those files, it gains deep knowledge of Remotion-specific idioms: how `<Composition>`, `<Sequence>`, and `<AbsoluteFill>` nest together; how `useCurrentFrame` drives animation; how to calculate timing without off-by-one frame errors. The result, according to both Remotion's documentation and independent testers, is production-quality output on the first attempt rather than iterative debugging.

The mechanism is deliberately model-agnostic. The same `npx remotion skills` command installs files that work with Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor — any agent that reads a project's skills directory. The instruction files themselves are open source in the `remotion-dev/skills` repository, so teams can inspect exactly what heuristics the AI is being given, or fork them for custom rigs.

The broader significance is a quiet expansion of what "vibe coding" — iterative, natural-language-driven development — can produce. Building UIs through conversation with an LLM is now commonplace; generating motion graphics and promotional video through the same loop is newer territory. Remotion Skills lowers the floor significantly: the workflow collapses to describing a video, letting Claude write the React, and calling `npx remotion render` to produce an MP4.

concepts.definition: Structured instruction files installed into a project's `.claude/skills` directory that teach AI coding assistants the best practices of a specific framework. They act as a curated knowledge layer on top of a model's general training, reducing hallucinated or incorrect API usage.

An open-source React framework, maintained by Remotion AG, for creating videos programmatically. Instead of a drag-and-drop timeline, developers write React components whose output is rendered to an MP4 or other video format. This makes videos reproducible, data-driven, and version-controllable.

Remotion's core animation primitives. `interpolate` maps a frame number to an output value (e.g., opacity 0 → 1 over frames 0–30). `spring` produces physically plausible easing curves — acceleration and overshoot — without manually tuning cubic beziers. Both are used with `useCurrentFrame`, which returns the current playback position.

repos.summary: The open-source repository containing Remotion's official Agent Skills instruction files. Installing from this repo via `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills` writes the files into `.claude/skills` in your project. Teams can fork the repo to customize the guidance given to their AI agents for proprietary video workflows.
